data.content_ref: inline:{"analogy":null,"claim":"As n grows, the probability of reaching unanimous consensus tends to a constant strictly between 0 and 1, not to 1 or 0.","counterconditions":[{"case":"If the random 3-regular graph has no short cycles (e.g. conditioned on girth growing with n), the small-cycle trap probability vanishes.","checker_spec":null,"eval":"observation"},{"case":"If the initial colouring has a large bias, the majority colour may overwhelm all seeds and consensus occurs.","checker_spec":null,"eval":"observation"},{"case":"If large matching traps contribute additional constant probability, the consensus probability could be lower than the small-cycle estimate.","checker_spec":null,"eval":"observation"}],"definitions":[],"derivation":[],"formalization_refs":[],"mechanism":"The cut size (number of bichromatic edges) decreases monotonically under asynchronous majority updates, so the process settles in a locally stable mixed configuration exactly when bichromatic edges form a matching. Small cycles are finite obstruction structures: a cycle of length L all minority with its L outside neighbours majority is stable because each cycle vertex has two same-colour neighbours and each outside neighbour has only one minority neighbour. The expected number of such cycle seeds of length L is (2^L/(2L))*2^(-2L)=2^(-L)/(2L); summing over L\u22653 gives a Poisson total \u03bb\u22480.034. With probability 1-e^(-\u03bb) a seed exists, and if the opposite colour wins globally (probability ~1/2) the process is trapped, so consensus probability is bounded away from 1.","premises":[],"schema":"deepreason-reasoning-envelope-v1","scope":{"covers":[],"excludes":[]},"simulation_refs":[],"uncertainties":[]}
